function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure thing! Here are some great ways to get a delicious cake delivered to your doorstep—whether you’re looking for a local bakery, a national chain, or an online specialty shop. | Option | What it offers | How to order | Tips | |--------|----------------|--------------|------| | **Local bakeries** | Fresh, often custom‑made cakes; great for supporting small businesses | • Call or visit the bakery’s website
• Many have online ordering or a phone line for special requests | • Ask about delivery fees or pickup options
• Check reviews on Google or Yelp | | **National cake delivery chains** | Consistent quality, nationwide coverage | • Visit the chain’s website (e.g., **Cake Boss**, **Baker’s Dozen**, **Tartine Bakery**)
• Use their online order form or call local store | • Look for “same‑day” or “next‑day” delivery options | | **Online specialty shops** | Gourmet, artisanal, or themed cakes (e.g., vegan, gluten‑free) | • Browse sites like **Goldbelly**, **Etsy (hand‑made cakes)**, **The Cake Delivery Co.**
• Select flavor, size, and delivery date | • Read shipping policies; some cakes ship in insulated boxes | | **Grocery stores & supermarkets** | Convenient, often with a “cake of the day” or pre‑made options | • Check the bakery section of stores like **Whole Foods**, **Trader Joe’s**, **Walmart**
• Many now offer online ordering through their websites or apps | • Some stores offer curb‑side pickup or delivery via services like Instacart | | **Meal‑delivery services** | Cakes included in meal kits or dessert boxes | • Sign up for services like **HelloFresh**, **Blue Apron**, or **Sun Basket**
• Look for dessert or cake options in the menu | • Great if you want a complete dessert experience | | **Local food delivery apps** | Same‑day delivery from nearby bakeries | • Use **Uber Eats**, **DoorDash**, **Grubhub**, or **Postmates**
• Search “cakes” or “bakeries” in the app | • Check delivery times and fees; some bakeries partner exclusively with one app | ### Quick Steps to Order 1. **Decide on the type of cake** (birthday, wedding, vegan, gluten‑free, etc.). 2. **Choose a provider** based on your location and budget. 3. **Place the order** online or by phone, specifying flavor, size, any custom text, and delivery date/time. 4. **Confirm payment** and any delivery instructions (e.g., “leave at front door”). 5. **Track the order** if the service offers a tracking number or delivery window. ### If You’re in a Specific City If you let me know your city or zip code, I can pull up a list of top-rated local bakeries and delivery services that operate in your area. Just drop the location, and I’ll give you a tailored list!
